exam_facts.question: How long is the grace period on an individual life policy in Wisconsin?
exam_facts.explain: 31 days. The policy stays in force; unpaid premium comes out of the death benefit.

exam_facts.question: What is the free-look period on an individual life policy in Wisconsin?
exam_facts.explain: 10 days (longer when the policy replaces another).

exam_facts.question: After how long does a life policy's incontestability clause take effect?
How much notice must a Wisconsin insurer give to cancel midterm, and to nonrenew?
exam_facts.explain: 10 days to cancel midterm, 60 days to nonrenew.

exam_facts.question: Wisconsin auto liability minimums are 25/50/10. Is uninsured motorist coverage required?
exam_facts.explain: Yes. UM is required at 25/50, bodily injury only.

exam_facts.question: A Wisconsin employer must carry workers comp with how many employees?
exam_facts.explain: 3 or more, or 1+ if wages reach $500 in a calendar quarter.

exam_facts.question: A $500,000 building is insured for $300,000 with 80% coinsurance. A $100,000 loss occurs. What does the insurer pay?

retake_facts.text: About 4 in 10 first-time Wisconsin insurance exam takers don't pass (58.1% passed in 2024).
Your emailed PSI score report includes a diagnostic of your strengths and weaknesses by topic.
In Wisconsin you can retest as soon as two days after a failed attempt, and there is no limit on attempts.
Your pre-licensing certificate is valid for one year from course completion, so you can retest without retaking the course inside that year.

retake_plan: Day 1: read your PSI diagnostic and list your two weakest areas.
Days 2-6: one weak area a day, 20 practice questions each.
Days 7-8: two full, timed 100-question practice exams.
Day 10: rest, then book the exam.
